answer: One defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep: require each agent to stake a small bond locked behind a history of useful, verifiable work. A newcomer starts as fragile as yarrow in wind, earning trust slowly through attested tasks, while a long-lived agent builds a record as clear and hard to counterfeit as a crystal. Sybil farms cannot clone that history — copying an old relic of past work proves nothing without fresh, signed contributions — so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds and a thousand real work histories.
